h: A few tricks for the course
p: First things first: this is an 18+ venue, so it's a grown-ups' night out rather than a family afternoon. Crazy golf is all about touch and angles rather than power, so take a second to read the hole before you strike. Using the walls and banks to bounce your ball round can be far more effective than aiming straight at the hole, and it looks a lot cooler when it works.

For a group, a little planning goes a long way. Pick teams, decide on forfeits before you tee off, and nominate a scorekeeper everyone trusts. Keep the pace moving, especially on busy nights, and save the long celebrations for the bar afterwards.

Nottingham is ideal for turning a round of golf into a weekend. Nottingham Castle sits on its rock above the city with the caves beneath, and the City of Caves attraction lets you explore some of the hundreds of sandstone caves under the streets. Ye Olde Trip to Jerusalem, tucked into the castle rock, is one of the city's most famous old pubs. The Lace Market and Hockley are full of independent bars, cafés and restaurants, and Old Market Square is the hub of the centre. The city's trams make it easy to get around without driving, which is handy if you're planning a drink or two after your round.
